title: Controlled Deviation Review, QA Boundaries and Disposition Handoff

content.overview: A strong deviation investigation preserves the procedure/version that governed the work, separates planned versus actual execution, states what is known and unknown, and hands the evidence to the authorized disposition role. Technician II can investigate and recommend verification without silently changing history or making independent release decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The controlled procedure version effective for the work at the time it occurred.
A preserved comparison between the authorized process and the execution/events that actually occurred.
The authorized decision governing release, rework, hold, destruction or another final product status.

sections.title: Use the version that governed the event
sections.body: Investigations must be able to retrieve the effective SOP/work instruction that applied at the time rather than judging past work only against a later revision.

sections.title: Do not repair history by overwriting it
sections.body: Corrections preserve original entries and explain the change. Planned values, actual values, deviations and later verification remain distinct.

sections.title: Investigation evidence supports but does not replace disposition authority
sections.body: The technician can summarize risk, scope and verification needs while the authorized QA/management role makes product release or disposition decisions.

workedExamples: The current SOP differs from the version active during the drying event; the investigation uses the historical effective version and documents the later change separately.
Evidence narrows the affected scope to two lots, but release remains pending; the technician hands off the genealogy, measurements and unresolved disposition question.
commonMistakes: Using the newest SOP to rewrite historical execution.
Overwriting planned values with actual values.
Releasing material because the technician believes risk is low.
content.practicalApplication: Create a QA-ready deviation package with governing procedure/version, facts, timeline, genealogy, affected scope, measurements, hypotheses, completed authorized actions and unresolved disposition questions.
content.summary: Controlled deviation work preserves historical truth and provides decision-ready evidence without exceeding release/disposition authority.

primaryVisuals.title: Controlled deviation review and disposition handoff
primaryVisuals.alt: Deviation review workflow identifying the governing procedure version at the time of the event, preserving planned versus actual execution and original corrections, summarizing facts, genealogy and measurements, and handing unresolved disposition questions to the authorized QA or management role instead of releasing product independently.
primaryVisuals.caption: Use the procedure version that governed the event, preserve planned and actual history, and hand final release, rework or destruction decisions to the authorized disposition role.
